docs.text: Webhook-Async Documentation ¶ A standalone Rust webhook receiver and asynchronous job engine. What is webhook-async ? ¶ webhook-async is a modern, memory-safe, standalone executable designed to receive HTTP webhooks and run tasks with complete reliability. It solves the two biggest challenges of traditional webhook infrastructure: 1. Preserving Upstream Compatibility : Full compatibility with adnanh/webhook v2.8.3 hook definitions, trigger rules, HMAC signatures, IP whitelists, and template preprocessing. 2. Eliminating Dropped Webhooks & Timeouts : Provides a durable, transactional queue engine (SQLite, Valkey, Redis) that commits jobs before acknowledging HTTP 202 Accepted , running tasks asynchronously with retries and concurrency limits. Core Features ¶ Single Self-Contained Binary : Written in pure Rust. No Node.js runtime, no Python, no mandatory Docker engine. Dual Execution Engine : Synchronous : Direct process execution returning stdout/stderr immediately; requires zero database or queue storage. Asynchronous : Durable queue committing an immutable execution snapshot before returning HTTP 202. Pluggable Storage Backends : SQLite (default): Embedded, WAL-mode, multi-threaded with busy timeouts. Valkey & Redis : Distributed scale-out using atomic Lua scripts and clustered hash-tagged keys. Integrated Web UI : Lightweight Askama server-rendered templates, HTMX reactive components, and Server-Sent Events (SSE). Hardened Process Execution : Commands run with an explicit argument vector (no shell string interpolation), process group isolation ( -pgid ), execution timeouts, and automatic temporary file cleanup. Dynamic Hot Reloading : Update hook definitions on the fly via SIGHUP , SIGUSR1 , or --hotreload polling with zero downtime. Define a Minimal Hook ( hooks.json ) ¶ [ { "id": "deploy-app", "execute-command": "/bin/echo", "pass-arguments-to-command": [ { "source": "payload", "name": "ref" }, { "source": "payload", "name": "commit" } ], "response-message": "Deployment initiated.", "include-command-output-in-response": true } ] 3. Run the Server ¶ webhook-async server --port 9000 --hooks hooks.json 4. Trigger the Webhook ¶ curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/hooks/deploy-app \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"ref": "refs/heads/main", "commit": "05dc3f3"}' Response: refs/heads/main 05dc3f3 Documentation Navigation ¶ Deployment Guide : Step-by-step guides for Linux (systemd), Docker Compose, Kubernetes, macOS (launchd), Windows, and Reverse Proxies (Caddy/Nginx). docs.text: REST API & Endpoint Architecture Reference ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • Configuration Reference • Operations 1. How Webhook Processing Works: The Complete Pipeline ¶ When an HTTP request hits webhook-async , it passes through a deterministic 10-stage execution pipeline before any command is executed or enqueued: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 1. Match Route & Method │ │ - Path: /{url_prefix}/{hook_id} │ │ - Check hook.http-methods (405) │ └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────────▼────────────────────┐ │ 2. Enforce Size & Content-Type Limits │ │ - Body <= max_body_bytes (413) │ │ - Parse Multipart parts (500) │ └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────────▼────────────────────┐ │ 3. Extract & Parse Payload Data │ │ - Preserve exact raw body bytes │ │ - Parse JSON, XML, or Form data │ │ - Execute parse-parameters-as-json │ └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────────▼────────────────────┐ │ 4. Evaluate Security & Trigger Rules │ │ - Check HMAC signatures (constant- │ │ time equality) │ │ - Check tokens, IP whitelists, regex │ │ - Mismatch -> HTTP 400 (or custom) │ └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────────▼────────────────────┐ │ 5. Build Immutable Execution Snapshot │ │ - Resolve command argv & environment │ │ - Materialize temporary files │ │ - Bind timeout and output limits │ └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘ │ ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐ │ │ [Sync Hook Branch] [Async Hook Branch] │ │ ┌────────────▼─────────────┐ ┌───────────▼────────────┐ │ 6a. Direct Execution │ │ 6b. Durable Commit │ │ - Spawn tokio::process │ │ - Commit snapshot to │ │ - Bound stdout/stderr │ │ SQLite / Redis │ │ - Clean up temp files │ │ - Dedup Idempotency │ │ - Return HTTP 200/500 │ │ - Return HTTP 202 │ └──────────────────────────┘ └────────────────────────┘ 2. Webhook Receiver Endpoints ¶ 1. Root Liveness Ping ¶ GET / Used by network load balancers, Kubernetes liveness probes, and reverse proxies. - Authentication : None required. - Response : 200 OK with plain text "OK" . - Headers : Includes global response_headers configured in config.toml . 2. Trigger a Webhook ¶ POST /{url_prefix}/{hook_id} Executes the hook identified by {hook_id} . - If url_prefix is configured as "hooks" (the default), the path is /hooks/my-hook . - If url_prefix is empty ( "" ), the path is /my-hook . - Subpaths are fully supported if your hook ID contains forward slashes (e.g. /hooks/deploy/prod/backend ). Supported Request Headers ¶ Header Description Content-Type application/json , application/x-www-form-urlencoded , text/xml , or multipart/form-data . Idempotency-Key / X-Idempotency-Key (Async hooks only) Unique request identifier. Prevents duplicate execution if a client retries due to network failure. X-Request-Id Distributed tracing request ID. Propagated through execution logs and responses. Exhaustive Response Status Codes ¶ HTTP Status Condition Response Body 200 OK Synchronous hook executed successfully. Output from stdout/stderr (if include-command-output-in-response: true ), or the configured response-message . 202 Accepted Asynchronous hook validated and committed to durable storage queue. {"job_id": "...", "status": "queued", "message": "..."} 400 Bad Request Trigger rules were not satisfied (HMAC mismatch, missing parameter, regex failure). "Hook rules were not satisfied." (or custom status code configured via trigger-rule-mismatch-http-response-code ) 405 Method Not Allowed Incoming HTTP verb (e.g. GET ) is not in the hook's http-methods list. Empty body. 413 Payload Too Large Request body size exceeds server.max_body_bytes . "Request body too large." 429 Too Many Requests Async queue capacity full ( queue.max_pending_jobs reached). {"error": "Queue capacity full."} 500 Internal Server Error Trigger rule evaluation failure, multipart parsing failure, or command exited with non-zero status. "Error occurred while evaluating hook rules." or command stderr output. 503 Service Unavailable In async mode, storage backend is unreachable. The hook was not acknowledged and must be retried by the caller. {"error": "Queue backend unavailable."} 3. System Diagnostic & OpenAPI Endpoints ¶ These endpoints provide health monitoring and schema inspection without requiring authentication. 1. Basic Health Check ¶ GET /api/v1/health Reports service availability and compiled application version. curl -s http://localhost:9000/api/v1/health { "status": "ok", "version": "0.1.0" } 2. Storage Readiness Probe ¶ GET /api/v1/ready Performs an active ping against the configured storage backend (e.g. SELECT 1 on SQLite or PING on Valkey/Redis). curl -s http://localhost:9000/api/v1/ready { "status": "ready", "storage": "connected" } If storage is disconnected, returns 503 Service Unavailable with {"status": "not_ready", "error": "..."} . 3. OpenAPI 3.1 Specification ¶ GET /api/v1/openapi.json Returns the complete machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 specification describing all REST endpoints, request schemas, response models, and authentication requirements. curl -s http://localhost:9000/api/v1/openapi.json | jq . 4. Administrative REST API ( /api/v1/* ) ¶ All administrative endpoints require Bearer token authentication configured via [auth].admin_token , [auth].admin_token_env , or [auth].admin_token_file . Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ADMIN_TOKEN> Security Guardrails : - If no admin token is configured in config.toml , all administrative endpoints return 503 Service Unavailable ("Admin token not configured"). Unauthenticated administrative access is strictly disallowed by default. - Rate limited to 60 requests/minute per token. Exceeding limits returns 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After: 60 . 1. Get Queue Statistics ¶ GET /api/v1/stats Returns real-time job counts partitioned across all 8 canonical job states. curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/stats { "counts_by_state": { "queued": 0, "running": 1, "retry_wait": 0, "succeeded": 412, "failed": 2, "cancel_requested": 0, "cancelled": 1, "dead_letter": 0 }, "pending_count": 1 } 2. List & Filter Jobs ¶ GET /api/v1/jobs?state={state}&hook_id={id}&limit={n}&offset={n} Query Parameters ¶ Parameter Type Default Description state string (optional) Filter by state: queued , running , retry_wait , succeeded , failed , cancel_requested , cancelled , dead_letter . hook_id string (optional) Filter by hook identifier. limit integer 50 Number of records to return (1 to 500). offset integer 0 Pagination offset. curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ "http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs?state=failed&limit=10" { "items": [ { "id": "018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f", "hook_id": "deploy-app", "state": "failed", "priority": 0, "attempt": 5, "max_attempts": 5, "created_at": "2026-03-29T10:15:30.123456789Z", "started_at": "2026-03-29T10:15:31.000000000Z", "completed_at": "2026-03-29T10:16:05.000000000Z", "worker_id": "worker-prod-1:4192", "exit_code": 1, "error_class": "transient", "error_summary": "Process exited with status: exit status: 1" } ], "total": 1, "limit": 10, "offset": 0 } 3. Get Job Details & Execution History ¶ GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} Returns complete metadata, immutable execution snapshot parameters, and the full audit trail of all execution attempts (including captured stdout and stderr previews). curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs/018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f { "job": { "id": "018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f", "hook_id": "deploy-app", "state": "succeeded", "priority": 0, "attempt": 1, "max_attempts": 5, "created_at": "2026-03-29T10:15:30.123456789Z", "started_at": "2026-03-29T10:15:31.000000000Z", "completed_at": "2026-03-29T10:15:45.000000000Z", "worker_id": "worker-prod-1:4192", "exit_code": 0 }, "attempts": [ { "job_id": "018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f", "attempt": 1, "worker_id": "worker-prod-1:4192", "started_at": "2026-03-29T10:15:31.000000000Z", "finished_at": "2026-03-29T10:15:45.000000000Z", "exit_code": 0, "stdout_preview": "Deploying release v1.4.2...\nMigration complete.\nService restarted.", "stderr_preview": "" } ] } 4. Retry a Job ¶ POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/retry Manually re-enqueues a job that ended in failed or dead_letter state. - Resets the job to queued state. - Automatically increments max_attempts so the job is eligible for immediate execution. - Returns 409 Conflict if the job is already active ( running or queued ). curl -X POST -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs/018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f/retry 5. Cancel a Job ¶ POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel Cancels a job: - If queued or retry_wait : Transitions immediately to cancelled . - If running : Transitions to cancel_requested . The active worker's heartbeat loop detects this state within milliseconds, sends SIGKILL to the child process group ( -pgid ), cleans up temporary files, and marks the job as cancelled . curl -X POST -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs/018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f/cancel 6. Inspect Active Hooks (Secrets Redacted) ¶ GET /api/v1/hooks Returns a list of all loaded hook definitions. Sensitive parameters (HMAC keys, bearer tokens) are safely redacted. curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/hooks 7. Inspect Active Workers ¶ GET /api/v1/workers Returns all background workers currently heartbeating into the cluster. curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/workers [ { "worker_id": "worker-prod-1:4192", "host": "ip-10-0-1-15.internal", "concurrency": 8, "active_jobs": 2, "completed_count": 894, "failed_count": 3, "draining": false, "last_heartbeat_at": "2026-03-29T10:20:00.000000000Z" } ] 8. Storage Engine Status & Capabilities ¶ GET /api/v1/storage/status Returns backend engine type, multi-host capabilities, and connection status. curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/storage/status { "backend": "sqlite", "connected": true, "capabilities": { "backend": "sqlite", "supports_priority": true, "supports_multi_host": false, "supports_idempotency": true } } 9. Real-Time Server-Sent Events (SSE) Stream ¶ GET /api/v1/events Streams live JSON snapshots of queue metrics and active jobs every 2 seconds. Used by monitoring tools and the built-in Web management UI. curl -N -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/events event: stats data: {"counts_by_state":{"queued":0,"running":1,"succeeded":412},"pending_count":1} event: stats data: {"counts_by_state":{"queued":0,"running":0,"succeeded":413},"pending_count":0}

The active worker's heartbeat loop detects this state within milliseconds, sends SIGKILL to the child process group ( -pgid ), cleans up temporary files, and marks the job as cancelled . curl -X POST -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs/018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f/cancel

docs.text: Configuration Reference & Step-by-Step Hook Guide ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • API Reference • Operations 1. Application Configuration ( config.toml ) ¶ webhook-async uses a single TOML file for server, worker, queue, storage, and security configuration. [server] host = "0.0.0.0" # Network interface to bind port = 9000 # Listening port url_prefix = "hooks" # Route prefix (e.g. /hooks/{id}) max_body_bytes = 10485760 # Maximum request body size (10 MB) max_multipart_mem_bytes = 1048576 # Memory buffer limit for multipart parts (1 MB) hook_files = ["/etc/webhook/hooks.json"]# Paths to hook definition files (JSON or YAML) hot_reload = true # Automatically reload hook files on change default_http_methods = ["POST"] # Fallback methods when hook omits http-methods response_headers = [ # Global response headers added to all replies { name = "X-Service", value = "webhook-async" }, { name = "Access-Control-Allow-Origin", value = "*" } ] use_x_request_id = true # Propagate or generate X-Request-Id header x_request_id_limit = 64 # Maximum character length for X-Request-Id trust_proxy_headers = true # Honor X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP for remote-addr [storage] backend = "sqlite" # Storage engine: "sqlite", "valkey", or "redis" [storage.sqlite] database_url = "sqlite:///var/lib/webhook-async/data.db?mode=rwc" wal_mode = true # Enable Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) for concurrency busy_timeout_ms = 5000 # Maximum wait time on busy database locks # Valkey / Redis configuration (uncomment when backend is "valkey" or "redis"): # [storage.valkey] # url = "redis://10.0.1.50:6379/0" # Accepts redis://, rediss://, valkey://, valkeys:// # key_prefix = "webhook_async:" # Namespaced key prefix (uses hash-tags for cluster) [worker] concurrency = 8 # Maximum concurrent background tasks poll_interval_ms = 250 # Delay between queue poll attempts when idle lease_duration_seconds = 60 # Lease window granted to worker for each claim heartbeat_interval_seconds = 15 # Frequency at which active worker extends lease shutdown_grace_seconds = 30 # Maximum drain duration on shutdown signal [queue] max_pending_jobs = 10000 # Maximum queued jobs (returns HTTP 429 when full) default_max_attempts = 5 # Maximum execution attempts before dead-lettering retry_base_delay_seconds = 5 # Exponential backoff base delay retry_max_delay_seconds = 300 # Exponential backoff ceiling delay default_timeout_seconds = 300 # Maximum execution time per command attempt max_output_bytes = 65536 # Maximum stdout/stderr output captured (64 KB) idempotency_retention_seconds = 86400 # Idempotency deduplication TTL (24 hours) [ui] enabled = true # Enable built-in Web management UI bind = "127.0.0.1:9001" # Dedicated bind for the Web UI path_prefix = "" # Optional URL subpath prefix (e.g. "/admin") [auth] admin_token = "password@123" # Direct literal password in TOML # Or load from an environment variable (or file path): # admin_token_env = "WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" # Or load from a dedicated secret file: # admin_token_file = "/run/secrets/admin_token" 2. Step-by-Step Guide: How to Configure hooks.json ¶ A hooks.json file is a JSON array of hook definition objects. Below is a progressive, step-by-step tutorial on building production-ready hooks. Step 1: The Absolute Minimum Hook (5 Lines) ¶ At its core, a hook only requires an id and an execute-command . Create a file named hooks.json : [ { "id": "hello", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/hello.sh" } ] When you start the server ( webhook-async server --hooks hooks.json ), calling: curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/hooks/hello will execute /opt/scripts/hello.sh and return 200 OK . Step 2: Set Working Directory and Restrict HTTP Methods ¶ In production, scripts should execute from an explicit directory and only allow intended HTTP verbs (typically POST ). [ { "id": "deploy-app", "execute-command": "/opt/app/scripts/deploy.sh", "command-working-directory": "/opt/app", "http-methods": ["POST"] } ] If an unauthorized method (like GET ) is sent, the server immediately returns 405 Method Not Allowed with an empty body and does not execute the command. Step 3: Customize HTTP Responses and Output Capture ¶ By default, the server returns an empty body on success. You can customize the response message or return stdout/stderr from the command directly to the caller. [ { "id": "ping-hook", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/check-health.sh", "command-working-directory": "/opt/scripts", "http-methods": ["POST"], "response-message": "Health check started successfully.", "include-command-output-in-response": true, "include-command-output-in-response-on-error": true, "response-headers": [ { "name": "Content-Type", "value": "text/plain" }, { "name": "X-Executed-By", "value": "webhook-async" } ] } ] include-command-output-in-response: true : The server waits for the command to finish and returns the combined stdout and stderr as the HTTP response body. include-command-output-in-response-on-error: true : If the command exits with a non-zero exit code, the HTTP response status becomes 500 Internal Server Error and includes the error output. Step 4: Pass Dynamic Arguments to Your Command ¶ Webhooks frequently receive payload data (commit IDs, branches, usernames) that must be passed as CLI arguments to your script. Use pass-arguments-to-command : [ { "id": "deploy-branch", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/deploy.sh", "command-working-directory": "/opt/scripts", "http-methods": ["POST"], "pass-arguments-to-command": [ { "source": "payload", "name": "ref" }, { "source": "payload", "name": "head_commit.id" }, { "source": "url", "name": "environment" }, { "source": "request", "name": "remote-addr" } ] } ] When a request arrives: curl -X POST "http://localhost:9000/hooks/deploy-branch?environment=production" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"ref": "refs/heads/main", "head_commit": {"id": "c759720"}}' webhook-async invokes: /opt/scripts/deploy.sh "refs/heads/main" "c759720" "production" "127.0.0.1" Security Note : webhook-async executes commands via direct process invocation ( execve ). Arguments are passed directly in the argv array and are never interpolated into a shell string, eliminating shell injection vulnerabilities. Step 5: Pass Values via Environment Variables ¶ Passing sensitive information or large payloads through environment variables is often cleaner than positional CLI arguments. Use pass-environment-to-command : [ { "id": "notify-slack", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/notify.sh", "pass-environment-to-command": [ { "source": "payload", "name": "pusher.name", "envname": "DEPLOY_AUTHOR" }, { "source": "header", "name": "X-GitHub-Delivery", "envname": "DELIVERY_ID" }, { "source": "payload", "name": "repository.name" } ] } ] Inside /opt/scripts/notify.sh , you can read: echo "Author: $DEPLOY_AUTHOR" echo "Delivery ID: $DELIVERY_ID" echo "Repository: $HOOK_repository_name" # Defaults to HOOK_<name> when envname is omitted Step 6: Write Payloads to Temporary Files ¶ When tools (like kubectl , ansible , or terraform ) require a file input, use pass-file-to-command . webhook-async creates a temporary file before execution, passes its absolute path in an environment variable, and automatically deletes it when execution finishes. [ { "id": "import-config", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/apply-config.sh", "command-working-directory": "/opt/scripts", "pass-file-to-command": [ { "source": "entire-payload", "envname": "CONFIG_FILE" }, { "source": "payload", "name": "certificates.ssl_crt", "envname": "CERT_PATH", "base64decode": true } ] } ] Inside /opt/scripts/apply-config.sh : echo "Applying config from: $CONFIG_FILE" kubectl apply -f "$CONFIG_FILE" Step 7: Secure the Hook with Trigger Rules ( trigger-rule ) ¶ Never expose unauthenticated webhooks to the public internet. Use trigger-rule to enforce signature verification, tokens, IP whitelists, or branch filters. Scenario A: GitHub / GitLab HMAC-SHA256 Signature Verification ¶ [ { "id": "github-deploy", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/deploy.sh", "http-methods": ["POST"], "trigger-rule": { "and": [ { "match": { "type": "payload-hmac-sha256", "secret": "{{ getenv \"GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET\" }}", "parameter": { "source": "header", "name": "X-Hub-Signature-256" } } }, { "match": { "type": "value", "value": "refs/heads/main", "parameter": { "source": "payload", "name": "ref" } } } ] } } ] Scenario B: Static Shared Secret / Bearer Token ¶ [ { "id": "internal-backup", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/run-backup.sh", "trigger-rule": { "match": { "type": "value", "value": "{{ getenv \"BACKUP_SECRET_TOKEN\" }}", "parameter": { "source": "header", "name": "X-Webhook-Token" } } } } ] Scenario C: Restricting Client IPs (CIDR Whitelist) ¶ [ { "id": "office-only-hook", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/restart.sh", "trigger-rule": { "match": { "type": "ip-whitelist", "ip-whitelist": "192.168.1.0/24 10.0.0.50 2001:db8::/32" } } } ] Step 8: Choose Synchronous vs. Durable Asynchronous Execution ¶ By default, webhook-async operates in legacy synchronous mode (the HTTP request waits until the command finishes). For long-running tasks (CI builds, deployments, backups), enable asynchronous mode : [ { "id": "async-ci-build", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/build-and-test.sh", "command-working-directory": "/opt/builds", "async": true, "response-message": "Job enqueued for background processing." } ] What happens when async: true : ¶ The server validates the trigger rules and signature. The server serializes the command and snapshot into the durable storage queue (SQLite, Valkey, or Redis). The server immediately returns HTTP 202 Accepted with a tracking JSON payload: json { "job_id": "018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f", "status": "queued", "message": "Job enqueued for background processing." } Background workers claim the job, execute it, heartbeat lease extensions, and handle automatic exponential backoff retries if transient errors occur. Step 9: Use Template Expressions ( -template ) ¶ To avoid hardcoding sensitive secrets or environment-dependent paths directly inside hooks.json , start webhook-async with the -template flag. Supported template functions: - {{ getenv "VAR_NAME" }} : Reads environment variable VAR_NAME (returns empty string if unset). - {{ getenv "VAR_NAME" "default_value" }} : Reads environment variable with fallback default. - {{ cat "/path/to/file" }} : Reads file content, trimming trailing newlines. - {{ credential "SECRET_NAME" }} : Reads /run/credentials/$SECRET_NAME (systemd credential directory), with fallback to environment variable. - {{ value | js }} : Escapes string safely for JSON string embedding. Example: [ { "id": "secure-hook", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/run.sh", "trigger-rule": { "match": { "type": "payload-hmac-sha256", "secret": "{{ cat \"/etc/secrets/webhook_hmac.key\" }}", "parameter": { "source": "header", "name": "X-Signature-256" } } } } ] Step 10: Validate Your Configuration ¶ Before deploying to production or reloading the service, validate your files with the built-in validator: # Validate standard JSON/YAML hooks webhook-async config validate --hooks /etc/webhook/hooks.json # Validate templated hooks webhook-async config validate --template --hooks /etc/webhook/hooks.json If errors are present (invalid rule depth, missing required fields, syntax typos), the command prints line-specific diagnostics with non-zero exit code. 3. Parameter Extraction Reference ( source ) ¶ Parameters can be extracted from any part of the HTTP request and mapped into command arguments, environment variables, temporary files, or trigger rule checks. Source Description Example Specification header Canonical MIME HTTP request header. Case-insensitive header lookup. {"source": "header", "name": "X-GitHub-Event"} url / query URL query parameter string. {"source": "url", "name": "environment"} payload Body value from JSON, XML, or Form payload. Supports dot notation ( a.b.c ) and array indices ( items.0.id ). {"source": "payload", "name": "repository.name"} raw-request-body The unparsed raw UTF-8 request body string. {"source": "raw-request-body"} request Request metadata: remote-addr (client IP) or method (HTTP verb). {"source": "request", "name": "remote-addr"} string Static literal string value. {"source": "string", "name": "production"} entire-payload The full raw body written to a temporary file ( pass-file-to-command ). {"source": "entire-payload", "envname": "BODY_FILE"} entire-headers JSON map of all HTTP request headers. {"source": "entire-headers", "envname": "HEADERS_JSON"} entire-query JSON map of all URL query parameters. {"source": "entire-query", "envname": "QUERY_JSON"} 4. Trigger Rule Combinators and Matchers ¶ Trigger rules determine whether the incoming request is authorized to execute the command. Combinators ¶ and : Array of rules; all child rules must evaluate to true . or : Array of rules; passes if any child rule evaluates to true . not : Inverts the boolean result of a child rule. Matchers ( match ) ¶ Matcher Type Description Required Fields value Constant-time string equality comparison. value , parameter regex Regular expression match against parameter value. regex , parameter payload-hmac-sha1 HMAC-SHA1 verification against raw request body. secret , parameter payload-hmac-sha256 HMAC-SHA256 verification against raw request body. secret , parameter payload-hmac-sha512 HMAC-SHA512 verification against raw request body. secret , parameter ip-whitelist Matches client IP against whitespace-delimited IPs/CIDRs. ip-whitelist scalr-signature Validates Scalr-compliant HMAC-SHA1 timestamp and signature. secret

docs.text: The server validates the trigger rules and signature. The server serializes the command and snapshot into the durable storage queue (SQLite, Valkey, or Redis). The server immediately returns HTTP 202 Accepted with a tracking JSON payload: json { "job_id": "018d9f10-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f", "status": "queued", "message": "Job enqueued for background processing." } Background workers claim the job, execute it, heartbeat lease extensions, and handle automatic exponential backoff retries if transient errors occur.

docs.text: To avoid hardcoding sensitive secrets or environment-dependent paths directly inside hooks.json , start webhook-async with the -template flag. Supported template functions: - {{ getenv "VAR_NAME" }} : Reads environment variable VAR_NAME (returns empty string if unset). - {{ getenv "VAR_NAME" "default_value" }} : Reads environment variable with fallback default. - {{ cat "/path/to/file" }} : Reads file content, trimming trailing newlines. - {{ credential "SECRET_NAME" }} : Reads /run/credentials/$SECRET_NAME (systemd credential directory), with fallback to environment variable. - {{ value | js }} : Escapes string safely for JSON string embedding. Example: [ { "id": "secure-hook", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/run.sh", "trigger-rule": { "match": { "type": "payload-hmac-sha256", "secret": "{{ cat \"/etc/secrets/webhook_hmac.key\" }}", "parameter": { "source": "header", "name": "X-Signature-256" } } } } ]

docs.text: Operations & Runbook ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • Configuration Reference • API Reference 1. Process Lifecycle & Signal Handling ¶ webhook-async handles standard POSIX signals for lifecycle events: Signal Action Behavior SIGHUP Reload Hooks Re-reads and re-validates hook definition files. Current active hooks remain untouched if parsing or validation fails. SIGUSR1 Reload Hooks Upstream-compatible reload signal. SIGTERM Graceful Shutdown Stops accepting new HTTP requests, drains workers for shutdown_grace_seconds , and cleanly unlinks PID/socket files. SIGINT Graceful Shutdown Intercepts Ctrl+C for clean termination. Sending Reload Signals ¶ # Using kill with PID file kill -HUP $(cat /var/run/webhook-async.pid) # Using systemd sudo systemctl reload webhook-async 2. Dynamic Hot Reloading ¶ When --hotreload is specified (or server.hot_reload = true in config.toml ), webhook-async polls the configured hook files for modifications every 2.5 seconds. Invariant Guarantees ¶ Atomic Swap : The internal routing table is updated atomically using a thread-safe read-write lock ( Arc<RwLock<...>> ). Immutable Job Snapshots : In-flight and queued jobs retain the exact ExecutionSpec snapshot captured when they were accepted. Reloading hooks never mutates running tasks. Fail-Safe : If a modified hook file contains invalid syntax or unknown fields, an error is logged and the server continues running with the previous valid configuration. 3. Logging, Diagnostics & Crash Safety ¶ Structured Logging ¶ Configure logging outputs: - Standard output: --verbose or --debug . - Dedicated log file: --logfile /var/log/webhook-async/service.log . Panic Immunity ( --nopanic ) ¶ In production, pass --nopanic (or -nopanic ). This installs a custom panic hook that logs the stack trace without aborting the server process, preventing individual malformed requests from causing an outage. docs.text: Security Architecture & Hardening ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • Configuration Reference • API Reference 1. Threat Model & Principles ¶ webhook-async receives untrusted payloads from the public Internet and executes administrative commands on internal infrastructure. Security is the paramount operational constraint. Foundational Principles ¶ Memory Safety : Written entirely in 100% safe Rust. No buffer overflows, use-after-free, or data races. Fail-Secure Defaults : Administrative endpoints require explicit token configuration. If unconfigured, access is rejected with 503 Service Unavailable . Zero Shell Interpolation : Commands are executed directly via OS system calls ( execve ) with discrete argument vectors. Payload strings are never evaluated by a shell interpreter. Constant-Time Verification : All cryptographic signatures and authentication tokens are validated in constant time to prevent timing side-channel attacks. Process Sandboxing : Command executions are assigned discrete process groups ( -pgid ), bounded by strict execution timeouts, and killed with SIGKILL on timeout or cancellation. 2. Process Execution Security ¶ Direct Process Execution vs Shell Injection ¶ Vulnerable systems often run webhook commands like this: # VULNERABLE: sh -c "deploy.sh --branch $BRANCH" # Payload: "; rm -rf / ;" In webhook-async , commands are invoked directly: let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&spec.executable); cmd.args(&spec.args); cmd.envs(&spec.env); Payload contents can only occupy designated discrete argument elements or environment variables. It is mathematically impossible for a payload value to inject additional command flags or shell operators. Process Group Sandboxing ¶ Child processes are launched in their own process group ( process_group(0) ). If execution exceeds queue.default_timeout_seconds or an operator cancels the task, webhook-async sends SIGKILL to -pgid . This guarantees that background subprocesses, sub-shells, or detached child processes are terminated immediately rather than orphaned. 3. Cryptographic Verification & Signatures ¶ Public webhooks should always enforce cryptographic signature verification using provider secrets. Supported HMAC verification matchers: - payload-hmac-sha256 (GitHub X-Hub-Signature-256 , Stripe) - payload-hmac-sha1 (GitHub legacy X-Hub-Signature , Bitbucket) - payload-hmac-sha512 - scalr-signature (HMAC-SHA1 Date + Body verification) Constant-Time Implementation ¶ All HMAC digests and tokens are verified using subtle::ConstantTimeEq : mac.verify_slice(&candidate_mac).map_err(...) Timing attacks attempting to deduce secrets byte-by-byte are mathematically defeated. 4. Web Management UI Security ¶ Session Tokens : Login issues a cryptographically random UUID session token stored in an HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax cookie. CSRF Tokens : Every mutation (Retry, Cancel, Logout) strictly requires a matching X-CSRF-Token header or form field. Strict HTML Escaping : Askama templates strictly escape all user-supplied variables by default, defeating Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Isolated Binding : The management UI can be bound to a separate IP/port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:9001 ) away from the public webhook receiver. 5. Security Checklist ¶ [ ] Run webhook-async as an unprivileged dedicated service account ( webhook ). [ ] Set WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN with at least 32 cryptographically random characters. [ ] Enforce HMAC signature validation on all public hooks. [ ] Bound execution timeouts ( queue.default_timeout_seconds ). [ ] Use direct TLS ( --secure ) or an authenticated reverse proxy (Nginx/Caddy) with HTTPS.

docs.text: Troubleshooting Matrix ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • Configuration Reference • API Reference HTTP Status Codes & Solutions ¶ Status Cause Resolution 400 Hook rules were not satisfied. Trigger rule mismatch (e.g. invalid HMAC secret, missing header, payload branch mismatch). Run server with --verbose to inspect trigger evaluation logs. Verify HMAC secret matches provider. 405 Method Not Allowed Webhook sent with an HTTP method not listed in hook's http-methods . Update hook's http-methods array or send the request using POST . 413 Payload Too Large Request payload exceeds server.max_body_bytes . Increase server.max_body_bytes in config.toml (default is 10 MB). 429 Queue capacity full In-flight queued jobs have reached queue.max_pending_jobs . Increase worker concurrency ( worker.concurrency ), add dedicated worker nodes, or increase queue.max_pending_jobs . 429 Rate limit exceeded Exceeded 60 requests/minute on administrative endpoints. Wait for the duration in Retry-After: 60 or throttle management scripts. 500 Internal Server Error Synchronous command returned non-zero exit code or rule evaluation threw an unhandled error. Inspect stdout/stderr in response (if include-command-output-in-response-on-error: true ) or inspect server logs. 503 Service Unavailable (On Hook Post) Storage backend is unreachable when accepting an asynchronous webhook. Check SQLite filesystem permissions or verify Valkey/Redis network connectivity. Webhook was not acknowledged. 503 Admin token not configured Calling /api/v1/* without configuring admin_token , admin_token_env , or admin_token_file . Set admin_token = "..." directly in config.toml , or set WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN in the environment. Worker & Execution Issues ¶ Job Transitions Immediately to dead_letter ¶ Cause : Executable path or working directory does not exist or lacks execute permissions. Why : webhook-async classifies missing binaries as non-transient Configuration errors and dead-letters immediately to prevent infinite retry loops. Solution : Use absolute executable paths (e.g. /usr/local/bin/deploy.sh ) and ensure the webhook user has read and execute permissions. Worker Heartbeat / Lease Expiry ¶ Symptom : Job stays in running and is reclaimed by another worker after 60s. Cause : Task process completely locked up the CPU or network, preventing the asynchronous heartbeat loop from renewing the lease. Solution : Ensure system resources are sufficient, or increase worker.lease_duration_seconds (e.g. to 120s). database is locked on SQLite ¶ Cause : High concurrency without Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) or missing busy timeout. Solution : Verify that wal_mode = true and busy_timeout_ms = 5000 are configured in [storage.sqlite] . Diagnostic Commands ¶ Validate Configuration Files ¶ webhook-async config validate --config config.toml --hooks hooks.json Check Storage Health ¶ webhook-async storage status --config config.toml Test Webhook Triggers Locally ¶ curl -v -X POST http://localhost:9000/hooks/test-hook \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"test": true}'
